answer: Identity is anchored in data custody, not stake. A joining agent gets a four megabyte seed file derived from its own key and never repeated elsewhere; each epoch a verifier issues twelve random byte-range queries to answer within two seconds. Missing two probes burns a thirty unit deposit, and the file cannot be rebuilt without the key, so each clone needs a live copy. Twelve probes over four megabytes stop one cache serving many accounts, and the ocean of probes grows with the fleet while the velvet of honest custody stays cheap. It is onyx-hard: the account has the bytes or it does not.
